observation.visible_scene: A top-down, close-up view of numerous hazelnuts scattered on a dark matte surface (slate-like), lit from one side so each nut casts a soft shadow. A loose, dense cluster occupies the center and right of the frame, while a few isolated nuts lie near the top-left edge.
visible_changes: The hazelnuts in the center and right of the frame stay completely at rest: their positions, orientations, and the orientation of their pale scarred bases are identical from the first to the last sampled frame.

In the top-left region, a small group of hazelnuts rolls slowly. Their orientation changes over time (the light circular base rotates into and out of view, e.g. from facing lower-right to facing down/up), and their positions shift slightly, with one nut drifting toward the top edge and partly leaving the frame.
The camera is fixed: the background texture and the shadows of the stationary nuts do not translate, so the observed shifts are object motion, not camera motion.
The rolling is gradual and continuous within the excerpt rather than a sudden tumble; the resting cluster shows no motion at all.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or onset of the top-left rolling (no trigger is visible inside the segment).
Whether the moving nuts come to rest or keep rolling beyond the crop boundaries.
Whether any nut entered the frame from outside the top edge during the excerpt.
uncertain_details: The exact count and individual trajectories of the rolling nuts are hard to follow because they overlap each other and cross the top frame edge.
A slight orientation change of the nut near top-center may be independent slow rotation or part of the same top-left motion; the excerpt does not disambiguate this.
